Now I have a clear understanding of the vulnerability. Let me analyze the `MQTT_PROP_TYPE_BINARY_DATA` case:

```c
case MQTT_PROP_TYPE_BINARY_DATA:
  if (i + 2 > end) return 0;                              // line 4156 (relative 48)
  prop->val.len = (uint16_t) ((((uint16_t) i[0]) << 8) | i[1]);  // line 4157 (relative 49)
  prop->val.buf = (char *) i + 2;                          // line 4158 (relative 50)
  new_pos += 2 + prop->val.len;                            // line 4159 (relative 51)
  break;
```

The bug: For `MQTT_PROP_TYPE_BINARY_DATA`, the code checks `if (i + 2 > end) return 0;` which only validates that the 2-byte length field fits. But it does NOT check that `i + 2 + prop->val.len <= end` (i.e., the referenced payload extent fits within the buffer). Compare with `MQTT_PROP_TYPE_STRING` which DOES have the check `if (i + 2 + prop->val.len > end) return 0;`.

So `prop->val.buf = (char *) i + 2;` points to a buffer of `prop->val.len` bytes, but if `prop->val.len` exceeds the remaining bytes, then later processing (in the fuzz harness, `mg_crc32(0, prop.val.buf, prop.val.len)`) reads beyond the input buffer.
